evidence.note: Ran the full suite and recorded '27 passed, 232 failed', mapping the failure set to test groups (NOA passing; EDA/BIF/alignment/analysis failing) — genuine periodic full-suite accounting.

Per-file 'ledger' contradicts itself: 'io/order.rs 12 methods, 0 todos' then later 'io/order.rs 2/12 methods'; 'io/factory.rs 12 methods 0 todos' then '2/12'. Tracking of done-vs-remaining was unreliable.
Recognized it had 'broke compilation' by changing the API and had to restore, but this began a repeated restore cycle rather than a controlled recovery.
Explicitly names the pathology — 'We need to stop the restore-implement-error cycle' — clear awareness of circular thrashing, but it does not escape it.

At the very end still 'restore skeleton' facing ~200 todos, having lost the earlier 27-passing state; believed prior sessions' work persisted when restores had undone it — net progress lost without detection.

reasoning: The agent periodically ran the whole suite and maintained a group-level sense of passing vs failing (above anchor 3), but its file-level ledger was inconsistent and, critically, it repeatedly wiped progress via 'restore skeleton' and lost track of whether earlier passes still held — regressing from 27 passing back to 0/~200 todos, the classic 'believe progress regressions undid' failure. It did notice the restore-implement-error thrashing (a higher-anchor signal) yet never changed tactic, so it never reliably caught regressions the way anchor 5 requires. This places it at a 4: better than occasional-runs-with-no-group-tracking, but well short of a working list that reliably catches regressions.
